references.html:1223:           <strong>Article use:</strong> Federal benchmark for interpreting the rent-burden percentages in the interactive. The 30% threshold is a housing-cost-burden benchmark, not a rule that every individual student must or should spend exactly 30% of income on rent.
references.html:1380:             <div class="fact-label">Why the threshold matters</div>
references.html:1381:             <div class="fact-value">HUD explains that a household paying more than 30% of income toward housing may have difficulty affording necessities such as <strong>food, clothing, transportation and medical care</strong>. The 30% line is therefore a cost-burden warning threshold, not a federal definition of comfort, financial security or “thriving,” and it does not mean households should aim to spend exactly 30%.</div>
references.html:1406:           <strong>Reporting language:</strong> Prefer “above HUD's 30% housing-affordability benchmark” or “above the 30% cost-burden threshold” over saying a student “fails the one-third rule.” The commonly repeated “one-third rule” is only shorthand; the federal benchmark used here is 30%.
